tagline: Systems programming: kernels, shells, assemblers and renderers — all running live in your browser.

apps.name: Kaname
apps.summary: A minimal x86 kernel in Zig: Multiboot2, GDT/IDT, PIC & LAPIC, PS/2 keyboard, VGA text + VBE framebuffer, serial console, ACPI shutdown, a tiny shell and a Phong-shaded 3D logo.
apps.how: Booted from a GRUB ISO by v86, an x86 PC emulator that JIT-compiles to WebAssembly.

apps.name: TraSH
apps.summary: A POSIX-style shell that compiles every command line ahead of time to bytecode run by a small VM: pipelines, && ||, subshells, redirections, heredocs, expansions, builtins.
apps.how: A real i386 Linux kernel + busybox userland booted in v86; fork, exec, pipes and signals are the kernel's own.

apps.name: Cub3D
apps.summary: A Wolfenstein-style raycasting engine: multithreaded renderer, fixed-timestep physics thread, lock-free triple-buffered world state, doors, minimap and a custom map format.
apps.how: C compiled to WebAssembly; pthreads run as Web Workers and MiniLibX is re-implemented on a canvas.

apps.name: FdF
apps.summary: A software 3D renderer for height maps: 8 projections (orthographic to Panini), Bresenham and Xiaolin Wu lines, face filling, depth view and back-face culling on a thread pool.
apps.how: C compiled to WebAssembly with a canvas-backed MiniLibX and a multithreaded rasterizer.

apps.name: zasm
apps.summary: A small assembler that turns a single source file into an x86-64 ELF executable, with syscalls by name and compiler-style diagnostics.
apps.how: The assembler runs as WebAssembly; its output is executed by a tiny x86-64 Linux sandbox written in JavaScript.
